title: Vulnerability Claim Adjudication Ledgers
description: Structural requirements for claim decomposition, per-assertion refutation evidence, the mechanical derivation of both verdicts, work-queue closure, and delivery discipline. Passing this schema does not prove a verdict is correct or that a maintainer will accept a report.

target.description: The target profile every verdict in this file is relative to: what kind of thing it is, its name, where its acceptance policy lives, and the channel it demonstrably uses.

kind.description: An open_source target carries the oss_verification block on every holding claim; the others state not-applicable in the notes section instead.

source.description: stated = the project published a policy; derived = the model was inferred from docs/history and the report must say so; none = nothing was found.

ref.description: The policy location, or a none-found statement naming what was searched.

preferred_channel.description: The channel the target's own advisory history shows it actually uses.

claims.description: One entry per claim under adjudication, with its decomposition, per-assertion verdicts, the derived validity and acceptability verdicts, and the action.

claim.description: The claim as received, in the words it was made.

claim_source.description: Where the claim came from: scanner, colleague, advisory, bounty report, our own reading.

source_ref.description: The source revision this verdict is relative to.

assertions.description: The claim split into parts that can each be true or false. A claim with no assertions is unadjudicated.

type.description: Which part of the claim this assertion is: the defect itself, that the attacker can reach it, the consequence that follows, or the precondition that must hold.

anchor.description: The file:line or concrete named fact this assertion is checked against.

verdict.description: confirmed = verified in source. refuted = the opposite was shown. unresolved = a decisive fact is not obtainable from source. fixed = the defect is absent from the current source.

refutation_attempted.description: The specific attempt made to kill this assertion and its result. An assertion with no attempt is unresolved, not confirmed.

absence_searches.description: Two distinct captured zero-match searches, required when a refutation attempt consisted of searching for a guard that does not exist, and required for an unresolved assertion that rests on search evidence alone. Re-running the same search is not a second check.

validity.description: Derived from the assertion verdicts, never asserted: any refuted -> does_not_hold; any fixed -> already_fixed; an unresolved defect, reachability or consequence -> needs_more_evidence; otherwise -> holds. An unresolved precondition does not block the validity: it says how easily the trigger fires, not whether the defect is there.

acceptance.description: Required when validity is holds. Never present for a claim that does not hold: such a claim is not a vulnerability, and is not 'unacceptable'.

divergence_sides.description: Both sides of a same-version behavioural divergence, each with file:line. Required when divergence_state is present.

divergence_absence_searches.description: Two distinct captured zero-match searches, required when divergence_state is absent.

oss_verification.description: Required on every holding claim when the target kind is open_source: the audit result checked one-by-one against the project's own record.

policy_verified.description: What the project's security policy / advisory history says about this claim's shape, with its reference.

introducing_commit.description: sha + date, or 'untraced — reason'. Never a guess.

released_in.description: First tag/release containing the defect, or untraced.

fix_state.description: none on main / fixing sha / partial.

published_as.description: Existing advisory/CVE covering this defect, or 'none found — searched …'.

historical_similar.description: Near-identical prior issues and how they were classified; the none-found entry (with what was searched) is a valid single item.

ref.description: GHSA/CVE id, commit sha, issue number, or the none-found statement.

classification.description: How the project itself classified the similar issue.

maintainer_preference.description: The project's demonstrated acceptance pattern (labelling, credit, cadence), with citations.

subject.description: The invariant the code fails to enforce. A consequence is not a subject.

original_subject.description: The consequence-framed subject this replaced, when a rewrite happened.

submission.description: Required when action is report or rewrite_then_report: the submission summary dimensions and the target list (references/submission-summary.md).

in_core.description: Is the defect in the product's advertised main line, or in a peripheral path?

evidence.description: What decides it: scope statement, module placement, default build.

aware.description: aware = a comment/TODO/issue shows the developers noticed this risk; false = searched, nothing; unknown = history unavailable.

special_config_required.description: Can the attacker reach the defect on the vendor's default, documented configuration? Must agree with the derived premise: true is rejected when the premise is attacker_only.

default_configuration.description: What the default actually is, cited.

from.description: The trust rung the attacker starts on.

targets.description: Where this claim can go. Exactly one entry is fit=primary; two primaries mean duplicate intake.

fit.description: primary = the one channel that receives the submission; secondary = viable, not first; unsuitable = rejected, reason recorded.

action.description: report = write the advisory. rewrite_then_report = write it with the rewritten subject. hardening_note = offer it as a patch, not a report. no_report = the claim was refuted. needs_evidence = a decisive fact is missing. already_fixed = the defect is gone.

artifact.description: Path to the artifact the verdict calls for.

work_queue.description: One bounded work item per claim plus a final review. At delivery, every item must be completed or explicitly deferred; active or queued work blocks delivery.

channel.description: Exactly one reporting channel. Two channels mean duplicate intake and read as spam.

coverage_paragraph_present.description: The notes file contains the coverage sections a reviewer scans to judge whether the adjudication was thorough.
